## Intent
Hypothesis: Halide-generated auto-vectorized math (loop1) can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads, with the simple scalar LP2 renderer adding only modest overhead.

## Cache saturation
The measured N range (10000–10000000) begins past the L2 spill (N≈7710). At death_q=0.01, ns/p stays FLAT from N=10000 to N=100000 (25.718 → 25.648), both L3-resident (working set 680 KB–6.8 MB vs 16 MB L3). A knee appears at the L3→DRAM spill (N≈246723): cost RISES to 30.04 ns/p at N=1000000 and stays FLAT at 29.078 for N=10000000. Death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape: at q=0.5 the flat region is 34.287–34.288 and the DRAM region is 37.2–37.4, preserving the same ~3 ns/p knee. The L1d (N≈481) and L2 (N≈7710) spills fall below the measured range and cannot be observed.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 2.65 GB/s at N=100000, death_q=0.01 — only 21% of the 12.69 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: frontend stalls dominate at 66–72% across all N and death rates, while backend stalls never exceed 12%. Bandwidth drops at the L3→DRAM transition (2.65 → 2.26 GB/s at N=1000000) but even the peak never approaches the ceiling. Death rate monotonically reduces peak bandwidth from 2.65 (q=0.01) to 1.98 GB/s (q=0.5), yet the bottleneck remains frontend overhead, not memory. No regime exists where the algo becomes bandwidth-bound.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize — the histogram reports zero vector-suffixed instructions. All floating-point work is scalar: `vmovss` for per-component loads (e.g., `vmovss xmm5,DWORD PTR [rcx-0x8]`), `vmulss`, `vaddss`, `vsubss` for arithmetic, and `vucomiss` for per-particle death checks. The math loop is dispatched to `halide_b5_math` via a single `call`, but the per-particle death/respawn/render loop that dominates runtime is entirely scalar. The render scatter uses byte-granular stores (`mov BYTE PTR [r13+r14*1+0x0],sil`) with saturating-add chains (`cmp`/`cmovae`/`movzx`), explaining the 66% frontend stall and the inability to stream. No packed data loads appear; the lone `vmovups` loads a constant.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 2.65 GB/s (21% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling) at any N or death rate. Zero vector instructions in the step function and 66–72% frontend stalls confirm the scalar per-particle death/render loop dominates, not the Halide math. The L3→DRAM knee raises ns/p from 25.6 to 30.0, but the algo remains overhead-bound throughout, never approaching bandwidth saturation.
